newsitem.title: ESTONIA: MAINOR TO PREPARE FOR BOURSE LISTING.
newsitem.headline: MAINOR TO PREPARE FOR BOURSE LISTING.

text.p: The shareholders' meeting of consultancy company Mainor on Monday decided to start preparations to list its shares on the Tallinn bourse.
"The decision was to prepare the listing...and the first step is to register the shares in the central depository," Mainor council chairman Ulo Parnits told Reuters.

Mainor share capital is 18.3 million kroons. Its major shareholders are Finnish investment company Finngulf Corporation with 25 percent, Maskello, a company of Mainor's employees, with 24 percent and the rest is held by Mainor's ex and present employees.
Parnits said that Mainor will probably issue new shares this year as it plans to get its shares listed at the beginning of 1998.
"We have possibilities to raise the share capital as the equity is supposed to double this year," he said.
Mainor had a net profit of 18.7 million kroons and turnover of 75.4 million kroons in 1996.
The company is also dealing with industrial projects and it is the major shareholder in one of Estonia's largest machinery factories, Dvigatel.
